latin: Ex mysterio trium litterarum quae sunt in dictione sciabat, id est, <Hebrew>, possumus interpretari cabalistice tunc sabbatizare mundum cum dei filius fit homo, et ultimo futurum sabbatum cum homines in dei filium regenerabuntur.
latin_note: The sheet's bracketed run '<NAW>' is Farmer's OCR rendering of the Hebrew spelling of 'sciabat' (shabbat), already named in the Latin itself; replaced here with '<Hebrew>' since the letters do not render (a parallel pass of the same page shows the run as '<N1W>', evidently the same OCR failure read twice, farmer1998:26710). The line-broken 'sabbatiza/re' is rejoined as 'sabbatizare', a hyphenation repair, not a variant word.
translation: From the mystery of the three letters in the word 'sciabat' (shabbat), that is, [Hebrew text], we may interpret cabalistically that the world then keeps sabbath when the Son of God becomes man, and that a last sabbath is to come when men shall be born again into the Son of God.
translation_note: 'sabbatizare' kept as 'keep sabbath' (to rest, in the manner of the Sabbath) rather than a single English verb; Pico ties this letter-mystery to the shin discussed the thesis before (11>14). 'sciabat' is Pico's transliteration of the Hebrew word; the Hebrew spelling appears only as a placeholder in the Latin field of this draft.
